sections.title: Agent Run Outputs
sections.description: ABB saves each execution as a separate attempt, including the test case, agent outputs, execution trajectory, and run status.

items.name: case.json
items.description: The exact test case used for this execution.

items.name: steps/<step>/
items.description: Each step's input.json, request.json, native result.json, and committed submission.json, together with captured traces.

items.name: trajectory.json
items.description: The derived execution trajectory, including model inputs and outputs and tool logs.

items.name: run.json · manifest.json · process.json
items.description: Execution status, step index, and configuration used for the run.

items.name: logs/
items.description: Execution and diagnostic logs. Additional workspace evidence is retained when produced.

sections.title: Issue Data
sections.description: Each issue directory contains a case definition (verify.case.json) and saved reference executions (runs/).

items.name: verify.case.json
items.description: A JSON file containing the issue report, tested version, reproduction steps, expected and observed behaviour, root cause, and fault locations. The example below shows the field names and value types; values are illustrative.

fault location.explanation: <why this location contributes to the failure>

items.note: steps is an ordered array of test inputs. pinned_contains_fix indicates whether the selected commit includes the fix. Field names are case-sensitive: "fault location" and "Root cause" include spaces. Available annotation details may vary between cases.

items.name: runs/
items.description: A directory of saved reference executions of this case. Each run preserves execution evidence such as trajectory.json (agent actions, model interactions, and tool calls), step inputs and results, and logs. These records show what happened when the failure was reproduced; the case definition and annotations are stored in verify.case.json.
